findings.en: {label} on — takes effect from your next turn / {label} off — calls will be refused until it is turned back on
findings.current: {label} activado — surte efecto desde tu próximo turno / {label} desactivado — las llamadas se rechazarán hasta que se vuelva a activar
findings.problem: Gender agreement is wrong in every render. The only values {label} receives are the two switch names built at app.py:42825 — 'búsqueda web' and 'consulta web' — both feminine, so the receipt reads 'búsqueda web activado' / 'consulta web desactivado'.
findings.suggestion: {label} activada — surte efecto desde tu próximo turno and {label} desactivada — las llamadas se rechazarán hasta que se vuelva a activar (a future masculine label would need a neutral shape, e.g. '{label}: activado')
findings.evidence: app.py:42824-42836 (label builders + the two receipt keys); the same two labels are the only values either template can receive

findings.problem: 'asentado' is a calque of 'settled' in its resting/established sense; the list it heads is the FINISHED goals (goal_panel.py paints them with _DONE_STYLE = Style(strike=True, dim=True), whose comment says the strike reads as 'finished'), so a reader can take it as 'goals that were set'. The in-flight tui.small catalogue prints the same heading as 'finalizados'. The only committed use of 'asentados' for settled (wire.settings, about projects being done/paused/archived) does not transfer to completed goals.
findings.evidence: local_operator/tui/widgets/goal_panel.py:_DONE_STYLE and 276; tui.small.goal_panel.settled_heading (untracked sibling, so NOT cited as shipped precedent); wire.settings.wakes_triggers_project_staleness_enabled.help

findings.en: attaches an image or file from the system clipboard / runs a named skill on the rest of the line / same, where the terminal forwards it; not Terminal.app
findings.current: adjunta una imagen o un archivo del portapapeles del sistema (60) / ejecuta una habilidad con nombre sobre el resto de la línea (59) / lo mismo, donde la terminal lo reenvíe; no en Terminal.app (58)
findings.problem: Every /help key row composes as name_width + note and the source pins the composed row at <= 74 cells at 80 columns (app.py:56210-56216, 56249-56265), with the cmd+v row documented as having ZERO headroom ('composes to EXACTLY 74'). name_width is 20 here, so these compose to 80, 79 and 78: each wraps, and the wrapped tail lands at the key gutter where it reads as another key row (design round 1 D2). A pinned test asserts the bound.
findings.suggestion: adjunta una imagen o un archivo del portapapeles (48 -> 68); ejecuta la habilidad indicada en el resto de la línea (53 -> 73); igual, si la terminal lo reenvía; no en Terminal.app (52 -> 72)
findings.evidence: app.py:56199-56600 (help block comments and the two cached-width tests); rich.cells.cell_len measurements in audit.log section B

findings.en: {shown} already leaving — asked again, then left alone
findings.current: {shown} ya saliendo — se les volvió a pedir y no se insistió más
findings.problem: The en phrase is deliberately count-neutral ('the phrase covers one and many, so only the digit varies' — sidecar); the es adds a plural indirect object, so with one session it reads '1 ya saliendo — se les volvió a pedir'.
findings.suggestion: {shown} ya saliendo — se volvió a pedir y no se insistió más (impersonal, count-neutral)
findings.evidence: tui.app.context.json note for this key; the string is rendered once for all counts (no ICU plural)

findings.en: same, where the terminal forwards it; not Terminal.app
findings.current: lo mismo, donde la terminal lo reenvíe; no en Terminal.app
findings.problem: Subjunctive reads hypothetical, but the fact is definite: this terminal does or does not forward the chord. Indicative is the natural mood, and the shorter wording also fits the row (APP-3).
findings.suggestion: igual, si la terminal lo reenvía; no en Terminal.app
findings.evidence: idiom; en states a condition on the terminal, not a hypothesis

findings.problem: 'consulta' in Spanish dev usage means query/request, so the pair 'búsqueda web' / 'consulta web' needs context to disambiguate; 'descarga web' or 'obtención web' names what the tool does. Current wording is distinguishable and matches house style, so this is preference.
findings.evidence: the two switch names are adjacent in the same receipt list

findings.en: runs a named skill on the rest of the line
findings.current: ejecuta una habilidad con nombre sobre el resto de la línea
findings.problem: 'con nombre' is a calque of 'a named skill' and reads as 'with a name'; the gesture runs the skill you name there. Fixed in the APP-3 replacement.
findings.suggestion: ejecuta la habilidad indicada en el resto de la línea

findings.en: retry budget exhausted / source retired / source left the screen
findings.current: presupuesto de reintentos agotado / origen retirado / origen fuera de pantalla
findings.problem: These three are consumed only by a logger.warning call (app.py:11503-11511), never by the sidebar panel. The glossary keeps developer logs English (allowlist category), so translating them puts Spanish into logs nobody localises. Catalogue-scope question, not a translator defect — the translations themselves are correct.
findings.suggestion: record the intent: either allowlist them as dev logs or accept translated log lines
findings.evidence: app.py:11499-11511; i18n/glossary.md section 1 (dev logs keep English); i18n/allowlist.toml
